reviews.text: Great, enjoyable and fun game. I've played this game since the demo and I must say the only complain I have is the fact that you can't scroll through your card binder with your keyboard. It's so nice to have a roguelike that plays like pokemon/magic tcgs. Other than that, this game released on my birthday, so thanks for this present.

I discovered the game two days before release and knew I had to get it. I'm someone who enjoys the mechanics of the Pokemon TCG but never got into it consistently. I'm proud to say that the game surpassed my expectations. Millennium Blades is one of my favorite board games because it replicates TCGs while being something you only need to buy once, so I really like the feedback loops and whatnot of them. I will admit it took me a few runs to really understand what was going on, but once I did I found the gameplay loop to be really rewarding and satisfying. I'm not really good at reviews, but I'd say if you enjoy TCGs but don't like how expensive they are, this is a great (albeit sometimes simple) way to get a similar experience.

Disclaimer: Played the ♥♥♥♥ out of the playtest since June 2024 If you like pokemon/Magic style TCG but don't want to get into multiplayer games (in my case is because i hate microtransactions) then, this game is for you. It's a SP TCG game with simple to learn yet hard to master mechanics, good balance and [b] no microtransactions whatsoever [/b] For us oldies that loved the OG pokemon TCG gameboy color game, this is the "re-mastered" version we always wanted

Isle of Swaps is a fun little Rogue-like throwback to those playground days of trading cards and playing big, flashy Pokémon. The system is simple to understand, and collecting the cards itself is fun. When you remember that it's over 400 cards without any microtransactions, then it really does hammer home how good of a deal it is. That said, once you've done everything, there isn't a great deal of replayability, but it still took me about 21 hours to get all of the achievements, and I had a blast while doing it. Also, the music is nothing but nostalgic fire.

In my opinion this game is edges on greatness but fails completely in one huge fundamental no way around it kinda way and that is how the game handles evolutions which we all know is a core part of any creature collection game we love to see our dudes evolve and become stronger and cooler than they were before and this mechanic is well established even in card game form looking at the obvious comparisons of and dare i say it's name lest nintendo sue me for copyright but pokemon and digimon. In those card games it all makes sense and flows you have all the creatures from that line in you're deck and you play the bigger ones on the smaller ones so they all have a purpose, however in this game while there are evolutions the evolutions function effectively the exact same as the pre evolutions, while they do have there own card effects what i mean is you don't need the prior evolution to get to the next one and the next one has no relevance to the previous one other than the art. Allow me to explain simply that your deck gets 3 pals, they can be any pals of any evolution and what colors they are make up the colors of your deck, that's it, you don't get to see you're guy evolve and become stronger mid game leaving a big hollow feeling in my chest every match, frankly this makes the game unplayable for me because of how wholly satisfying it is. My solution would of course require a rebalance of the game but you're deck should be made up of 3 base pals and evolutions should be cards you put in your deck to play on top, it would need testing to feel right but the evos could have a range of mechanics attached to them -more hp -on play effects -a cost you have to pay to play the card And in general should be a better version of the pre evolution as would make sense rather than completely doing it's own thing with some exceptions. So in conclusion with this fundamental part of the game being a complete fail in my opinion i can not recommend this game though it does have some really fun concepts The swapping/trading is a really cool mechanic It's fun to open boosters Some of the special battles like the rival could be made to be a little more something something but overall are cool And the binder is incredibly fun to collect and flip through. With that baste i have one final gripe that could be overlooked but it's annoying that the ai does not play by the same rules as you do, they play the same number of cards but they don't need energy for there moves that can sometimes lead to you being attacked relentlessly though they still do play energy’s sometimes.

Isle of Swaps is a very cute card game Roguelike, not in the Slay the Spire sense, but in a "that trading card game that was popular at school but you only got one or two packs of cards a week" sense. The main game mode has you progressing through challenges starting with a very thin deck of available cards and gradually building up a workable deck primarily by trading cards with defeated opponents. The default character has an advantage while trading, and each opponent will list a type of card they're interested in which are worth extra points, and you really need to put those edges to work in order to trade up, getting rid of cards you don't plan to use in exchange for carefully chosen ones you're sure you will. It creates a very fun dynamic as you progress through each run, and encourages coming up with a plan and sticking to it. For those who like their trading card games less random and more constructed, at the end of each run you also "master" all of the cards in your deck and several that were stuck in your binder, allowing you to use them in an alternate game mode where you build a deck of mastered cards and just play through three opponents without any of the roguelike elements. These battles seem a bit on the easy side (or it's possible I've just already constructed a broken deck), but nonetheless provide a fun format to play the game as well. Overall, this game is very cute and very compelling, I see myself playing plenty more of it :)

《集换岛》（Isle of Swaps）是一款由Fuzz Force制作并发行的Rougelike牌组构建游戏，游戏结合了集换式卡牌游戏的最大特点“交换”以及宝可梦式的宠物组合玩法，通过使用卡牌战斗和收集构建卡组组成更加强大的队伍挑战截然不同的敌人，虽然游戏画风粗糙，但玩法和创意相当不错，适合喜欢卡牌收集类的玩家一试。 游戏的主要玩法是参加一场卡牌挑战赛，通过所收集各种卡牌完成随机的战斗以及boss，在挑战过程中，可以不断用新收集到的卡牌、技能和生物来组成强大的构筑牌组，提升自己的实力。整个战斗流程一共有三个等阶，难度依次提升，如果三个阶段都取胜则代表玩家称为挑战赛冠军。 游戏的对战模式类似于3V3的宝可梦对战，每回合有着固定的抽牌数，但每位玩家每回合只能出三张技能卡牌，通过合理的组合搭配来帮助队伍赢下战斗是游戏的核心。不同宠物之间还有着属性区别，而使用招式也需要获得对应的属性能量，因此就规定玩家在构建牌组过程中需要平衡获取能量和输出能量的关系，虽然卡牌的效果大多简单易懂，但是要想组成一幅强大的队伍还是颇费脑筋的。 在牌组构建过程中主要的卡牌获得方式为抓捕野生宠物获得的自带卡牌、商店购买单独卡牌、贩售机开包以及和战败的选手进行交换这几种方式，需要注意的是一定要多去购买和开包，毕竟和其他人对战本身是不获得任何卡牌的，仅交换很快把通用卡牌换走之后就没有库存来进行交换了，尤其是稀有卡需要6个点数，因此在路线中就要规划好获取卡牌和交换的平衡。 虽然游戏本身的画风可爱，卡牌设计精美，玩法新颖，但也不妨碍游戏还是存在一些缺点，譬如官中错漏较多，内容体量偏少等，尤其是游戏本身没有难度等级的设定，仅仅只有两种不同的玩法选择，而且游戏使用一些强力宠物通关后会变成精通生物，可作为初始宠物进行选择，导致后期难度实在不高。不过客观来说整体上瑕不掩瑜，尤其是刚开始玩的几个小时体验很好，期待制作组委后续带来更多有趣的新鲜内容。 总而言之《集换岛》是一款结合了怪物收集和Rougelike卡牌游戏元素的作品，适合喜欢卡牌游戏和策略游戏的玩家。游戏的卡牌交换机制和丰富的策略性玩法为玩家提供了深度的游戏体验，尽管游戏在内容和难度上可能还有待提升，但其创新的玩法和精美的卡牌设计已经值得喜好此道的朋友浅试一二。 [quote] 游玩百态，将游玩心得用汉语化作玩家的指明灯，(๑•̀ㅂ•́)و✧ [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402408/]点击这里关注汉化语录~[/url] 如果喜欢这个评测，请点个赞让更多人看见 [/quote]

Cute! Not huge or too complex (100%ed after about 20 hours), but this game very much captures the nostalgic appeal of gradually amassing a collection of trading cards. The game's biggest strength is that you're rarely locked into a strategy. You can (usually) see the elements of the next opponent, and can change your entire deck between every battle, which very much encourages making a dragon hoard of cards. Other pluses are the adorable critters (with artist credit!) and clear element identities. If the cards had flavor text, it would hit all of my weaknesses. The biggest miss is probably the sheer randomness of battle turns. You can see what moves your opponent will make, but sometimes an enemy will burst you down with 3 attacks on turn 1 before you can set up, and other times they'll use a card that does literally nothing. Losing to a fluke is made all the more painful by the fact that you lose a critter if you lose a battle, and then have no choice but to try the same battle again. Other minor gripes are with a lack of polish in some areas. I had a few overlapping menu glitches, and hiding the ability to click a button to move through the binder (instead of swiping) in the settings menu is awkward when there are so many pages to flip through. Overall, I enjoyed my time with it! If you don't already like roguelike deckbuilders and don't have any connection to the feel of old playground TCG gameplay, this probably won't make you fall in love, but it hits the mark pretty well for me.

This game is fine. It's not particularly bad, and as you can see from my hours, it's pretty playable and interesting. However, the reason that this game drops to a Not Recommended, is because the UI is horrible: - "Flipping" through your collection feels like it's built for a mobile device. - Once an hour or so the UI bricks and you just can't click anything, requiring an Alt-F4. - Some cards are terribly written and don't make sense until you play a couple of times with them. If there was a "Meh", review rating, I'd give it that, but I can't, and I definitely don't recommend it. It's fine.

Very fun game, interesting combos, various strategies are playable but ... the game is just too easy. I guess developers didn't want the game to be frustrating but basically "lives" are not used at all because at some point you just stop losing. Since you don't loose Nuzzlelock becomes just normal mode without additional challenge. Randomiser challege is just a big joke, since it's easier than default mode, you just take duo monsters and exploit "super effective" bonus. Additionally strategies like spamming AoA, just using energy cards if you get true damage from them are just OP. To speed up every mode (except nuzzle lock) you can just spam "white flag" card. As I said it's too easy but I still played to max everything, so I guess it was worth it.
